title: Normal bundle and zero section
statement:
In the purity conventions of this chapter ([def-pur-conventions] fixed setting),
let $i:Z\hookrightarrow X$ be a closed immersion with ideal sheaf
$\mathcal I$. The *normal cone* is
$N_{Z/X}=\operatorname{Spec}_Z\bigl(\bigoplus_{r\geq0}\mathcal I^r/ \mathcal I^{r+1}\bigr)$; if $i$ is a
regular immersion of pure
codimension $c$, the conormal sheaf
$\mathcal I/\mathcal I^2$ is locally free of rank $c$, and
$N_{Z/X}\to Z$ is a *vector bundle* of rank $c$ with a canonical
*zero section* $z:Z\hookrightarrow N_{Z/X}$.

Here the ideal sheaf is that of [def-sbc-closed-immersion-ideal-sheaf] and its powers are [def-sbc-ideal-sheaf-powers]. The displayed direct sum is the quasi-coherent graded $\mathcal O_Z$-algebra $\mathcal G$ of [lem-pur-conormal-graded-algebra], so the spectrum is the relative spectrum of [lem-weil-pbc-affine-morphism-relative-spec]. The notation $\mathcal I/\mathcal I^2$ on $Z$ means the conormal module $\mathcal C=i^*\mathcal I$ [def-pc-module-pullback], not an $\mathcal O_X$-module regarded without change as a sheaf on $Z$. Locally free of rank $c$ is [def-amb-finite-locally-free-module], and vector bundle with zero section is [def-pur-vector-bundle-zero-section]; its zero section here is induced by the projection $\mathcal G\to\mathcal G_0=\mathcal O_Z$.

proof.text: Take the quasi-coherent conormal algebra $\mathcal G$ supplied by [lem-pur-conormal-graded-algebra]. This supplies its multiplication, its $\mathcal O_Z$-algebra structure, the degree-zero identification with $\mathcal O_Z$, and the degree-one identification with $\mathcal C=i^*\mathcal I$. In particular the direct sum appearing in the definition is a sheaf algebra on $Z$: on $X$ its degree-$n$ pushforward is $\mathcal I^n/\mathcal I^{n+1}$, whereas on $Z\cap\operatorname{Spec}R$ it has algebra of sections $\operatorname{gr}_J(R)$ for the defining ideal $J$.

Apply [lem-weil-pbc-affine-morphism-relative-spec] to the conormal algebra and its degree-zero augmentation. The resulting arrow is a morphism in the over category, so its over-category equation gives the section identity. The projection is affine, and its composite with the section is the identity, hence a closed immersion. Mathlib IsClosedImmersion.of_comp therefore makes the section a closed immersion. This proves zeroSection_spec without a separate affine-cover calculation.

source.place: Tag 0636 (definition-normal-cone); relative spectrum is constructions.tex Tag 01LX (lemma-spec-properties), and closedness uses morphisms.tex Tag 01QO (lemma-closed-immersion)

proof.text: Now assume $i$ is regular of pure codimension $c$. The part of [def-pur-regular-immersion] used here is precisely that $X,Z$ are finite type over $k$ and that for each $z\in Z$ the ideal $J_z\subset R_z=\mathcal O_{X,i(z)}$ is generated by an $R_z$-regular sequence of length $c$; the claimed smooth-pair equivalence in that node is not used. The field $k$ is Noetherian, since its ideals are $0$ and $k$, generated by $0$ and $1$. Therefore [lem-weil-pbc-finite-type-over-noetherian] makes $X$ and $Z$ Noetherian. By [lem-pur-conormal-graded-algebra], $\mathcal C=\mathcal G_1$ is coherent and $\mathcal C_z=J_z/J_z^2$. Apply [lem-weil-pbc-regular-sequence-conormal-free] in $R_z$: these stalks are free of rank $c$ over $R_z/J_z=\mathcal O_{Z,z}$. The coherent free-stalk criterion [lem-sc-coherent-free-stalks-locally-free] makes $\mathcal C$ finite locally free. Its local rank is $c$: a rank-$r$ trivialization at $z$ yields $\mathcal C_z\cong\mathcal O_{Z,z}^r$, and reduction modulo the maximal ideal compares vector-space dimensions $r=c$. This proves the exact conormal-rank assertion.

source.place: Tag 063M (lemma-quasi-regular-immersion), rank argument at stalks; algebra.tex Tag 00LN (lemma-regular-quasi-regular), degree one; local freeness via algebra.tex Tag 0GWM (lemma-finitely-presented-localization-free)

proof.text: Use the canonical comparison and its constant and generator formulas from [lem-pur-conormal-graded-algebra]. At a point z transport the regular-sequence basis from [lem-weil-pbc-regular-sequence-conormal-free] along the conormal stalk equivalence and the quotient-ring equivalence. Mathlib SymmetricAlgebra.equivMvPolynomial identifies its symmetric algebra with the polynomial ring on this basis [lem-weil-pbc-symmetric-algebra-free-module-polynomial]. Every conormal stalk element has a representative on the inverse image of an affine open of X: choose a germ, refine its neighborhood using the closed embedding, and use [lem-weil-pbc-affine-conormal-sections] and the surjective cotangent quotient. The comparison therefore sends each polynomial variable to the corresponding degree-one associated-graded class and sends each constant to its degree-zero class. MvPolynomial.ringHom_ext identifies it with the map of [lem-pur-regular-sequence-graded-polynomial], after changing coefficients by the quotient-ring equivalence. That map is bijective, so the comparison is an isomorphism at each stalk. The ideal-equality transport and the polynomial comparison are proved as private algebraic helpers before specialization to stalks; these introduce no new assumed results.

Apply Mathlib TopCat.Presheaf.isIso_of_stalkFunctor_map_iso directly to the comparison of commutative-ring sheaves. The forgetful functor from the under category reflects isomorphisms, so the canonical algebra comparison is an isomorphism. Apply the relative-spectrum anti-equivalence [lem-weil-pbc-affine-morphism-relative-spec] to it; together with the finite locally free conormal module of Step 3, this constructs exactly the vector-bundle datum of [def-pur-vector-bundle-zero-section] on the already defined normal cone. Its over-base compatibility is Over.w. No global frame is chosen.

The augmentation of $\operatorname{Sym}(\mathcal C)$ in [def-pur-vector-bundle-zero-section] fixes constants and sends every degree-one generator to zero. The composite $\epsilon\psi$ has these same two properties, since $\psi$ preserves degrees and $\epsilon$ is projection to degree zero. Uniqueness in [lem-weil-pbc-quasi-coherent-symmetric-algebra-core] makes these algebra maps equal. Contravariance of the anti-equivalence [lem-weil-pbc-affine-morphism-relative-spec](3) says precisely that the isomorphism of Step 5 carries the section $z$ of Step 2 to the vector-bundle zero section. This proves its canonicity and compatibility with the displayed normal-cone construction.

proof.text: For the actual extended-Rees cone, use the existing normalConeToQuotientSpec map. Its composite with the quotient-scheme structure map is the cone-to-X map, and the latter quotient map has kernel I. Thus I is contained in the kernel of cone-to-X. Define its canonical lift through the closed immersion. If g retracts i, compose lift_fac with g and use i followed by g equals the identity to recover normalConeProj. This factorization is independent of the comparison with the relative-Spec normal cone.

split_report.summary: Expanded the implicit O_Z typing of the conormal algebra; constructed the actual relative spectrum and its augmentation section; proved conormal local freeness using existing regular-sequence and free-stalk nodes, then proved the full symmetric-algebra identification on stalks and matched augmentations. Created only two unsplit supporting algebra statements, searched by the prescribed command. NormalConeData is explicitly not tied to the immersion and is not an attachment.
split_report.blueprint: The defining Spec_Z formula and both regular-immersion clauses in the statement of the blueprint node, also the normal-cone sentence of sk-def-purity-conv; the unit has no proof steps to replace. Steps 1-2 construct the cone and section, Step 3 proves the conormal rank, Steps 4-6 prove the vector-bundle and zero-section identification.

tool_uses.why: Finite-type schemes over the Noetherian field k are Noetherian; this generic finiteness tool is not a purity theorem.
The regular generating sequence gives the degree-one basis at each stalk; no node of this unit states that ring lemma.
Coherent modules with free stalks are locally free; this generic local algebra tool proves the sheaf assertion without replacing any unit step.
Converts a conormal basis into polynomial coordinates on its symmetric algebra; generic algebra tool.
Transports the standard free-module symmetric-algebra identification to the chosen basis by its generator formula.
Detects the canonical symmetric-to-conormal algebra map as an isomorphism via its underlying sheaf of modules.
Constructs the normal cone and sends the algebra comparison and augmentation to scheme morphisms.
Proves closedness of the augmentation section from its surjective maps on affine charts.
Identifies the two augmentations by the symmetric-algebra universal property.
